concept.name: Backtest
concept.definition: A historical simulation that applies explicit strategy rules to past data to estimate how the strategy would have behaved under stated assumptions.
concept.intuition: It turns an informal trading idea into a claim or design choice that can be evaluated against dated evidence.
concept.mechanics: Advance through dated observations, form decisions from the contemporaneous information set, simulate orders and costs, and update cash and positions.
concept.failure_modes: Results can mislead when hindsight, multiple testing, nonstationarity, costs, or unavailable historical information are ignored.
concept.misconceptions: A favorable historical result is evidence about the tested sample and assumptions, not proof of a durable profitable edge.
concept.example: A monthly momentum rule is replayed from 2010 through 2020 with delisted stocks, next-open fills, fees, and slippage.
